sessions.title: Fire safety and evacuation
sessions.blurb: What to do on discovering a fire, the alarm, evacuating guests, and keeping escape routes clear.
sessions.legal: Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, art. 21: staff must be given suitable fire safety instruction and training on induction, and again when risks change.
sessions.external: Fire marshals need a separate practical course.

sessions.title: Slips, trips and falls
sessions.blurb: Wet floors, cables, stairs and clutter: how everyone spots and removes the hazards that cause falls.
sessions.legal: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, reg. 13 (training on induction and when risks change).

sessions.title: Manual handling
sessions.blurb: Lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling safely: kegs, laundry, trays, furniture and luggage.
sessions.legal: Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992: avoid hazardous handling where possible, assess the risk, reduce it, and train people.
sessions.external: Practical coaching on the job should follow.

sessions.title: First aid awareness and reporting accidents
sessions.blurb: Who the first aiders are, what to do in an emergency, and how every accident, injury and near miss is recorded.
sessions.legal: Health and Safety (First-Aid) Regulations 1981; RIDDOR 2013 (reporting of injuries, diseases and dangerous occurrences); the accident book (Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1979).
sessions.external: First aiders need a recognised First Aid at Work or Emergency First Aid at Work course from a competent training provider.

sessions.title: Dignity at work: equality and preventing harassment
sessions.blurb: Treating colleagues and guests fairly, spotting harassment (including by guests), and how to raise it.
sessions.legal: Equality Act 2010, including the duty to take reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment of staff (s. 40A, in force 26 October 2024).

sessions.title: Data protection and guest privacy
sessions.blurb: Looking after guest, couple and colleague information: what we collect, how to keep it safe, and what to do when something goes wrong.
sessions.legal: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018: staff handling personal data must understand how to protect it.

sessions.title: Safeguarding and spotting exploitation
sessions.blurb: Children and vulnerable guests, and the signs of modern slavery, trafficking and child exploitation in a hotel or venue.
sessions.legal: Good practice rather than one statute: Children Act 1989 and 2004, Modern Slavery Act 2015, Sexual Offences Act 2003. Staff should know the signs and who to tell.

sessions.title: Security awareness and suspicious behaviour
sessions.blurb: Spotting the unusual, what to do about unattended bags and unwelcome visitors, and how to act in a serious incident.
sessions.legal: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 (duty of care); the Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025 (Martyn's Law) is being phased in for venues, so staff awareness is good practice now.
sessions.external: The free ACT Awareness e-learning is a good addition.

sessions.title: Food hygiene essentials
sessions.blurb: Personal hygiene, handwashing, cross-contamination, cleaning and keeping food safe from delivery to plate.
sessions.legal: Food Safety Act 1990; Regulation (EC) 852/2004 Annex II ch. XII: food handlers must be supervised and instructed or trained in food hygiene matters appropriate to their work; Food Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013.
sessions.external: Anyone preparing food should also hold a Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate.

sessions.title: Allergen awareness
sessions.blurb: The 14 allergens, taking and passing on allergen information, avoiding cross-contact, and what to do in an emergency.
sessions.legal: Food Information Regulations 2014 (14 allergens, information for non-prepacked food); Food Information (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2019 (Natasha's Law, from 1 October 2021).
sessions.external: Staff handling or serving food should also hold a recognised allergen certificate.

sessions.title: Temperature control and food safety records
sessions.blurb: Fridge, freezer, cooking, hot-holding and cooling temperatures, and the daily records that prove them.
sessions.legal: Regulation (EC) 852/2004 art. 5 (procedures based on HACCP principles) and the temperature control requirements in Food Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013.

sessions.title: Safe use of kitchen equipment, knives, burns and scalds
sessions.blurb: Slicers, mixers, fryers, hot liquids and knives: using them safely and what to do when it goes wrong.
sessions.legal: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998 (PUWER); Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999; Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974.

sessions.title: Dealing with drunken guests and refusing service
sessions.blurb: Recognising drunkenness, refusing service calmly, handling the aftermath and keeping everyone safe.
sessions.legal: Licensing Act 2003: s. 141 (selling alcohol to a person who is drunk), s. 140 (allowing disorderly conduct), and the premises licence conditions.
sessions.external: The designated premises supervisor must hold a personal licence.

sessions.title: Age-restricted sales and Challenge 25
sessions.blurb: Alcohol and other age-restricted sales: checking ID properly, refusing, and keeping the refusals log.
sessions.legal: Licensing Act 2003 s. 146 and 147 (selling alcohol to children, and allowing it), s. 147A (persistently selling), and the mandatory age verification policy condition.

sessions.title: Conflict, aggression and lone working
sessions.blurb: Keeping calm with an angry guest, protecting yourself, and staying safe when you work alone or late.
sessions.legal: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999 (risk assessment, including violence and lone working); HSE guidance on work-related violence and lone working.

sessions.title: Cellar safety: kegs, CO2 and gas
sessions.blurb: Working safely in the cellar: CO2 leaks, moving kegs, pressure and the checks before you go in.
sessions.legal: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; COSHH 2002 and the workplace exposure limits for carbon dioxide (EH40); Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000; Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992; HSE guidance on CO2 in cellars.

sessions.title: Turning and flipping mattresses and bed-making
sessions.blurb: Making beds and turning mattresses without injury: team lifts, the right technique and when to ask for help.
sessions.legal: Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992; Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999; HSE guidance on reducing musculoskeletal injuries in housekeeping.

sessions.title: Cleaning chemicals and COSHH
sessions.blurb: Reading labels and safety data sheets, mixing nothing, wearing the right protection and what to do after a splash.
sessions.legal: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002 (COSHH): information, instruction and training for anyone who uses or is exposed to hazardous substances.

sessions.title: Working at height and ladders
sessions.blurb: Stepladders, ladders, platforms and step stools: choosing the right one, checking it and using it safely.
sessions.legal: Work at Height Regulations 2005: avoid work at height where possible, use suitable equipment, and ensure people are competent.

sessions.title: Legionella and water safety awareness
sessions.blurb: Why water that sits still is a risk, flushing unused rooms and outlets, shower heads and what to record.
sessions.legal: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; COSHH 2002; HSE Approved Code of Practice L8 (control of legionella bacteria in water systems).
